extra_differences: Capture path: Record B's OpenLIT command installs hooks into both agents (`openlit coding install --vendor=claude-code` and `--vendor=codex`, content capture default `full`) beside the OTLP exporters both agents already have; under the no-install default the native exporters own capture and the hooks are not installed. Record B pass 1 keeps two stores with two query surfaces (agent sessions in OpenLIT, service metrics in Prometheus), although OpenLIT's docs say its Metrics explorer lists every OTel metric it receives; the record does not say which store owns Claude Code's native token and cost metrics.

OpenLIT's release and its current docs describe different ingest designs: tag 2.1.0 bundles otelcol-contrib v0.142.0 under an OpAMP supervisor, while main documents a first-party OTLP receiver and says the image does not ship otelcol. `ghcr.io/openlit/openlit:latest` and `:2.1.0` had the same digest on 2026-10-02, so the compose installs the bundled-collector build today.

Port contention: OpenLIT's compose publishes OTLP on host ports 4317 and 4318, the ports Record B also gives the Collector (`openlit configure --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:4318`); neither pass says which process owns them.

Off-host usage reporting is on by default in Grafana and Loki (`reporting_enabled`, stats.grafana.org), OpenLIT (PostHog, `TELEMETRY_ENABLED`) and Phoenix (`PHOENIX_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`); neither record lists the opt-outs that a local pipeline needs.

Temporality: Claude Code exports delta metrics by default and Prometheus handles OTLP deltas only behind the experimental `otlp-deltatocumulative` flag; set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE=cumulative`. Neither record states it.

Collector install path: Record B builds it from source (`make otelcontribcol`, the CONTRIBUTING local-testing target); upstream's Linux install page says every Collector release includes DEB and RPM packaging. Record A gives no command.
result.notes: Gates were read as written, so all five candidates pass; OpenLIT's ClickHouse pin counts under moving parts, not as a gate failure. Rule 3 was applied per job, as written. Metric transport: Record A scrapes the Collector's Prometheus exporter, Record B names none; Prometheus's OTLP receiver is off by default, and Claude Code exports delta temporality by default while Prometheus's delta conversion is experimental.

Pins and install path: Record A pins Collector v0.162.0 and Prometheus v3.15.0 and builds the Collector from source (make otelcontribcol); Record B carries no pins or commands; opentelemetry.io documents v0.162.0 release packages.

items.reasons: Rule 1: provider usage is the reference side of the requirement's measurement clause, so the job is in scope, but it already has owners. Claude Code: `/usage`, headless JSON usage, OTel `claude_code.token.usage`. Codex: `/status`, `/usage daily|weekly|cumulative`, `codex exec --json` usage, OTel `codex.sse_event` token counts and the `turn.token_usage` metric. OTel Collector Contrib can receive both over OTLP. ccusage re-reads the same local files. Rule 2: the fetched ccusage pages report no evaluation against provider records; its guide says costs are estimates. Rule 3: gates pass (v20.0.26, 2026-09-27; CI success via gh; `npx ccusage@latest`), but its Codex source is labelled experimental. A clean host has no pre-telemetry backlog. Docs fetched 2026-10-02.

evidence.quote: ccusage reads local usage data from coding agent CLIs and turns it into daily, weekly, monthly, and session reports.
| `/usage` | Show session cost, plan usage limits, and activity stats.
3. To open token activity directly, type `/usage daily`, `/usage weekly`, or `/usage cumulative`.
| `claude_code.token.usage` | Number of tokens used | tokens |

items.measurement: Run matched Claude Code and Codex sessions on this host (interactive, headless, with subagents) with OpenTelemetry export on. Compare per-session and per-day totals per token class from (a) native sources: `claude -p --output-format json` usage, `codex exec --json` `turn.completed` usage and the collector's series; (b) `ccusage daily --json` and `ccusage session`; reference: provider-side usage records for the same requests. Metric: absolute token error per class and sessions missing. Install ccusage only if (a) cannot give complete per-session totals for both agents and (b) matches the provider within tolerance.

resulting_layer.owners: mise: reproduces the selected tools and their configuration from the repository-carried bootstrap (lockfile, `mise bootstrap`). Restic: backs up and restores application state, with explicit paths and excludes keeping authentication stores out. chezmoi and Devbox are not installed.

No installed tool. Context supply: none (settled by measurement). Provider usage: Claude Code and Codex native usage commands and JSON usage output, plus their OpenTelemetry token data through OTel Collector Contrib (telemetry layer, configuration only). ccusage, agent-console and sqz are not installed.

extra_differences: recovery-portability: Devbox (pair pass 2 only) competes for tool reproduction, the job the task settles on mise; its README says it is "internally powered by `nix`", an extra substrate, and neither pass shows a measured gain: not installed.

recovery-portability: the passes differ on Restic's install command (`mise use -g restic@0.19.1` vs `sudo apt-get install restic`); Restic's 0.19.1 documentation lists `mise use -g restic@latest`, so the mise route is upstream-documented and the 0.19.1 pin is pass 1's substitution.

recovery-portability: both pair passes record that neither tool enforces authentication-store exclusion by itself (it rests on Restic paths and excludes); the single record carries no such acceptance condition.

token-efficiency: sqz (pair pass 2 only) is a context compressor, the context-supply job already settled as none by measurement; its README calls its replay savings an estimate: outside the final set.

token-efficiency: agent-console (pair pass 2 only) does the same after-the-fact usage job as ccusage and adds a local console process on 127.0.0.1:6787; same overlap with the native counters, more moving parts: not installed.
token-efficiency: pair pass 1 selected nothing and deferred every candidate because its page fetches were blocked, so the pair record's selection rests on pass 2 alone.

token-efficiency: for the ccusage versus agent-console comparison, pass 1 names complete provider records as the reference and pass 2 names identical raw usage records; only provider-side records can test accuracy, since both tools read the same client logs.
token-efficiency: the single record's row title "the usage meter only" presumes a meter; with ccusage not installed the layer holds no installed tool.
result.notes: Pages fetched 2026-10-02 through Context Mode; quotes re-read from the same URLs. One gh call (GraphQL): chezmoi, ccusage, mise and Restic heads show CI SUCCESS, none archived.
